about.how.s1: A new round opens every Monday, and everyone who joins picks their free times for the week.
about.how.s2: Once enough people join, you get suggestions ranked by shared interests, goals and overlapping free time. You can also browse everyone by tags.
about.how.s3: Tap "I'd like to meet" on anyone. If they say yes too, it's a match; if they skip, nobody gets notified.
about.how.s4: After a match you both see each other's contact details and shared free times — tap one to lock it in, and tell us afterwards whether you met.
about.how.title: How matching works
about.name.text: Yalelux = Yale + lux, Latin for "light" — from Yale's motto, Lux et Veritas (Light and Truth). We'd like it to work like a lamp: lighting up Yalies scattered around the world and bringing them together.
about.name.title: The name
about.not.chat.sub: Once you both say yes, use WeChat, email — whatever you already use.
about.not.chat.title: No in-app chat
about.not.feed.sub: Nothing to scroll, nothing pushed at you.
about.not.feed.title: No feed
about.not.intro: Yalelux is about meeting a few real people, not another app to scroll.
about.not.likes.sub: It's not a contest for the biggest network.
about.not.likes.title: No likes, followers or connection counts
about.not.title: What we left out on purpose
about.now.text: One round a week: fill in a profile, pick a few free times, and we'll suggest a few people you might click with — or browse by tags yourself. When you both tap "I'd like to meet", you swap contact details and grab a coffee, in person or online. Every so often there's a themed Coffee Chat week or month.
about.now.title: First up: Coffee Chat
about.privacy.ai.p1: The site and its database run on a server in the United States. If you use Yalelux from mainland China, your information is transferred abroad.
about.privacy.ai.p2: Smart ranking is optional. When it's on, we send anonymised answers — student or alum, stage, class year, questionnaire answers and your one-line intro, under a temporary ID — to DeepSeek, a company in China, to help order your suggestions. Your name, emails, contact handle, job and city are never sent.
about.privacy.ai.p3: You can turn it off under "Me" anytime; you'll then get rule-based suggestions only (shared interests, goals and free times) and nothing is sent. Your intro is free text, so please keep contact details and your full name out of it.
about.privacy.ai.title: Smart ranking and cross-border data
about.privacy.changes.text: When anything changes, the version number goes up and we'll ask you to agree again before you continue. We record which version you agreed to and when.
about.privacy.changes.title: When this notice changes

about.privacy.collect.title: What we collect
about.privacy.contact.text: Questions about privacy, or want to see or delete specific data? Leave a note in the feedback box and an ACSSY volunteer will follow up.
about.privacy.contact.title: Contact us
about.privacy.delete.p1: You can delete your account under "Me" anytime. Deletion is immediate and removes your profile and contact handle, your free times in every round, all invites and matches you sent or received, suggestion records, and sign-in sessions.
about.privacy.delete.p2: The activity log keeps only an anonymous user ID, for security audits. For now, addresses in the email log, the email and network address recorded when you requested codes, and your feedback notes aren't removed automatically — if you'd like them gone too, tell us in the feedback box before you delete your account.
about.privacy.delete.title: Keeping and deleting
about.privacy.email.code.sub: Only when you ask, at most 5 an hour. Can't be turned off.
about.privacy.email.code.title: Sign-in and verification codes
about.privacy.email.digest.sub: Bundled into a digest, at most one every 24 hours. Optional.
about.privacy.email.digest.title: Someone wants to meet you
about.privacy.email.event.sub: One when each event starts. Optional.
about.privacy.email.event.title: Event kickoff
about.privacy.email.intro: Notifications go to your contact email (or your Yale email until it's verified). Each one is in Chinese, then English, and never includes anyone's contact details.
about.privacy.email.match.sub: One per match. Always on, so you don't miss it.
about.privacy.email.match.title: It's a match
about.privacy.email.reminder.sub: A heads-up for both of you the day before. Optional.
about.privacy.email.reminder.title: Meeting reminder
about.privacy.email.scheduled.sub: When the other person picks or changes the meeting time. Always on.
about.privacy.email.scheduled.title: Time set
about.privacy.email.title: Emails
about.privacy.email.unsub: Every optional email has a one-click unsubscribe link at the bottom — no sign-in needed — and you can switch each type on or off under "Me" anytime. Emails go out through a delivery service (such as Resend, in the US), which handles your address and the message content.
about.privacy.email.weekly.sub: Every Monday when a new round opens; skipped during events. Optional.
about.privacy.email.weekly.title: Weekly email
about.privacy.intro: In plain words: what Yalelux collects, who can see it, where it's stored, and how you stay in control.
about.privacy.security.audit: Every change — sign-ins, profile edits, invites, replies, scheduling, publishing events, account deletion — is recorded in an audit log.
about.privacy.security.cookie: Your sign-in token lives only in an httpOnly cookie that page scripts can't read. The server stores just a hash of it, so even a leaked database can't be used to sign in.
about.privacy.security.secrets: Secrets live only in the server's environment, never in the code repository.
about.privacy.security.title: Security
about.privacy.see.admin.what: ACSSY volunteers. They see aggregate numbers, the feedback box (with submitters' names), the email log (without addresses) and the activity log (user IDs only) — never your contact handle, emails, detailed answers or invite notes.
about.privacy.see.intro: You can always see all of your own data. Everyone else:
about.privacy.see.invited.what: All of the above, plus your note.
about.privacy.see.mutual.what: All of the above, plus your contact handle (e.g. WeChat) and the time you agree on.
about.privacy.see.nobody.what: Your sign-in codes, who you skipped, and your email addresses — no other user or admin can see these.
about.privacy.see.others.what: Your name, a one-line identity (e.g. "Master's · Class of 2027"), your public questionnaire answers, and the free times you share.
about.privacy.see.server.what: Can technically access the whole database, so server access is limited to one or two people.
about.privacy.see.title: Who can see what
about.privacy.summary: We collect only what coffee matching needs; your contact details go only to people you've both said yes to; smart ranking and most emails can be switched off, and you can delete your account anytime.
about.privacy.title: How we handle your information
